contract.boundaries: Verify timezone, daylight-saving conversions, clock precision and same-t ties. Events equal to t are not known; promise effective_at=t may apply only when observed_at<t.
contract.coverage: Separate raw valid approval denominator, joined orders, known true-event register, timestamp-valid events, and as-of covered query/history windows. Missing true-event or revision denominator means actual capture rate unknown, not 0%.
contract.decision_rule: No accepted additional as-of event/version source means pending_data_no_training. Absence within inspected sources is not global non-existence.
contract.event_rule: Require stable order identity, event type/semantics, occurred_at<t AND observed_at<t. Closure here means cancellation or another non-delivery transition that exits the risk set; existing delivery completion timestamps remain a different known event. Source received time and project persisted/ingested time must be distinguished and independently explained.
contract.joins: Verify same anonymized order_id or an authorized mapping, key uniqueness, one-to-many version cardinality, orphan events, conflicting versions and overlapping validity intervals. Seller-only linkage is insufficient.
contract.ordering: Report missing/invalid timestamps, duplicates/conflicts, event order, observed-before-occurred anomalies, late-arrival/backfill delays and immutable revision policy. A promise may be observed before its future effective time.
prohibited_substitutes: Final exported status or final single promise value
CSV mtime or later local database import/binlog time as original observed_at
Review dates or shipping deadlines as cancellation/promise revisions
A seller marketing closed-deal as an order closure
API indexed examples as acquired authorized historical same-ID data
contract.promise_rule: Require promised value, version identity, effective/valid time, observed/system time, supersession/correction/retraction history. Select only observed_at<t versions effective_at<=t and valid under what was known at t.
contract.query_clock: t is the current query approval time, not each historical order own approval. Cancellation may follow historical approval and still precede t.
contract.scope: Verify each query month and required historical lookback, including route/promise/approval-week/support coverage. Do not import future events or rescore original holdout.
contract.snapshot_alternative: Immutable complete snapshots require captured_at, available_at<t, cadence and completeness proof. They can establish known status as of a snapshot under a separately accepted contract, not exact cancellation occurrence time.

database.interpretation: Configured project database visible metadata only; orders is the identical final eight-column CSV snapshot. Zero visible metadata objects does not prove inaccessible schemas/accounts have no data. Local creation/import timestamps are not original source observation times.

limitations: Bounded inspected local/public sources only; no global non-existence claim.
No actual original ingestion, cancellation/closure or promise revision source was accepted; actual capture rates remain unknown.
Private evidence JSON represents this executed inventory snapshot; live services/files are not queried or refreshed on rerun.
No training or new prediction experiment; existing historical validation/development recall and untouched holdout status are unchanged.

local_inventory.binlog_interpretation: Only prior file/header evidence is bound, not live files. These 2026 local import events are not 2016-2018 original order observed_at; table row-event counts are not source-event or order counts. No SQL or row payload is published.

json_metadata_inventory.meaning: Top-level key screening is a bounded metadata check, not proof that every value has been exhaustively excluded as event evidence.

local_inventory.permission_scope: Denied and explicitly skipped directories were not read; do not count them as source coverage. No inaccessible path names are published.

acceptance_requirements: Stable order identity linked to this cohort.
Event type and valid event time, including cancellation/closure semantics.
Source-observed/received time and project ingested time with timezone and ordering semantics.
Original promised value and revisions with version id, effective/valid time and observed/system time.
Actual coverage by approval week, route, promise and support volume; delay distributions and late-arrival/backfill policy.
catalog_search_limits: Targeted searches found the two known Olist-owned datasets; user-filtered Kaggle list endpoints returned an empty array and an organization datasets URL returned 404. These outcomes were not treated as a complete owner catalog or proof that no other official source exists.
Third-party copies, educational pipelines and synthetic SCD/ingestion timestamps were not accepted as original Olist historical observation evidence.

official_public_sources.reporting_boundary: No new source has met the project acceptance contract within the inspected sources. This is a bounded not-yet-obtained finding, not a global non-existence claim. Keep daily 10%, five seeds and frozen models; perform zero new fits until real source data and as-of provenance are accepted.
official_public_sources.scope: Known Olist-owned Kaggle e-commerce dataset, its linked Olist marketing funnel dataset, and official Olist developer documentation discoverable through targeted primary-source web searches. This is not an exhaustive proof about all possible sources.

availability.meaning: Zero verifiable new cancellation/non-delivery-exit clocks or promise versions, not zero actual events. Existing delivery completion timestamps are present but lack ingestion times. A non-null single exported promise is not proof of its approval-time version.

orders.scope: Final statuses are retrospective descriptors only, never an as-of event or feature. No final status filter. Invalid approval timestamps cannot enter a pre-cutoff cohort; no outcome/performance aggregates after cutoff.
